L'adenocarcinoma duttale è una massa ipo:
Ductal adenocarcinoma is an ill-defined hypodense (hypovascular) mass, best seen in the late arterial (pancreatic) and portal venous phases. Tumors of the tail do not cause jaundice and are found late, when they are large.
The report must include: site and size; relationships with the arteries (celiac trunk, superior mesenteric artery, common hepatic artery) and with the veins (superior mesenteric and portal), described as contact of less or more than 180° and as deformity or occlusion; adjacent organs (spleen, stomach, adrenal gland, colon); lymph nodes; liver and peritoneal metastases. From these comes the category: resectable, borderline or locally advanced.
In the current TNM classification (AJCC 8th edition) T4 indicates involvement of the celiac trunk, superior mesenteric artery or common hepatic artery, regardless of size.
Incidental findings, such as a valve prosthesis, must always be reported: they change the surgical risk and the management of anticoagulation.
